name: Όρμος Υστερνίων
evidence: Travel piece on Ormos Ysternion Tinos: visitors sit 'κάτω από τα αλμυρίκια και τις ψάθινες ομπρέλες' — straw umbrellas on the beach, fish tavernas right on the water; no explicit sunbed rental mention.

name: Παραλία Σταυρός
evidence: Described only as a small picturesque beach near Chora good for afternoon swims; no source states sunbeds/umbrellas or a bar at this beach (heavy name collision with Stavros Crete/Chalkidiki).

name: Κέδρος
evidence: Kedros Donousa explicitly 'δεν έχει ομπρέλες και ξαπλώστρες' but has a beach bar/canteen on the beach serving coffee, drinks and food all day; camping/nudism friendly.

name: Λουτρό
evidence: Koufonisia guides: 'καμία δεν είναι οργανωμένη' with the exceptions of Fanos and Ammos — Loutro (a boatyard/port cove) is not among them.

name: Παναγία
evidence: Kato Koufonisi is described as undeveloped/natural; beaches there have no facilities (only the taverna by the Panagia harbor), and island guides state no organized beaches besides Fanos/Ammos on Ano Koufonisi.

name: Πόρι
evidence: Pori is explicitly not organized ('δεν είναι οργανωμένη με ομπρέλες και ξαπλώστρες' — shops for coffee/food are above the beach); in 2026 the state suspended licensing for canteen/sunbeds at Pori and Italida.

name: Φοίνικας
evidence: Finikas Koufonisia 'is not organized with loungers or umbrellas'; a small restaurant sits just above the beach.

name: Λιόλιου
evidence: Lioliou Schinoussa is an organized beach with umbrellas/sunbeds (free sunbeds) and a beach bar; the Grispos Villas/Lioliou Beach Hotel complex operates there.

name: Ψιλή Άμμος
evidence: Sources describe a popular sandy beach on Schinoussa but none explicitly mention sunbeds/umbrellas or a bar (heavy Psili Ammos name collision across islands).

name: Λιβάδι
evidence: Local Iraklia site: Livadi has a few tamarisks and advises 'it is good to have a means of shading with you' — no sunbeds/bar mentioned; naxospress describes it as loved by free campers. (Beware collision with organized Livadi on Ikaria.)

name: Άγιος Βασίλειος
evidence: astypalaia-island.gr describes it as quiet/peaceful with shade from big trees; no mention of sunbeds/bar, contrasted with 'more cosmopolitan and organized' Livadi, but not explicitly called unorganized.

name: Κούνουπες
evidence: Boat-access double beach on the Kounoupes islet: 'a beach bar offers the basics', but no shade and it is not organized with loungers — bring your own equipment.

name: Λιμάνι Παναγιάς
evidence: Municipality of Karpathos lists Limani Panagias (Lefkos) as 'Organized beach with umbrellas and taverns'; other guides note it has a few umbrellas and sunbeds (not enough for everyone).

name: Μακρύγιαλος
evidence: No Karpathos-specific source found confirming facilities; the municipal all-beaches page does not list a Makrygialos, and search results collide with Makrygialos in Pieria (Central Macedonia).

name: Μανδράκι
evidence: Kastellorizo's only small pebble beach; mixed reports that the municipality placed a few sunbeds/umbrellas and of a swim platform with umbrellas, but the accounts are garbled and may refer to other spots on the islet.

name: Πλάκες
evidence: Plakes is a slippery-rock swimming spot; the organized swimming area with sunbeds and a small taverna on Kastellorizo is on the Agios Georgios islet, not Plakes — no explicit statement about Plakes facilities.

name: Παραλία Καρνάγιο
evidence: Kos guides: Karnagio (before Tigaki) 'is not considered organized, so it's likely you won't find crowded sunbeds'; quiet family beach with shallow water.

name: Παραλία Λάμπη
evidence: Lambi Kos is well organized with sunbeds, umbrellas and showers at all organized sections, plus seafront restaurants/bars, water sports and beach volley.

name: Προτοκάραβος
evidence: Protokaravos (Kefalos, Kos) 'is organized with umbrellas and sunbeds in some areas', divided into two sections, otherwise quiet and wild.

name: Πλατύς Γιαλός
evidence: Lipsi guides state that rentable umbrellas, loungers and canteens are not permitted on any beach of Lipsi, including Platys Gialos; only a taverna at one end of the beach.

name: Άσπρη
evidence: Patmosweb lists Aspri without any facilities or organization mention; no source found stating sunbeds or a bar.

name: Σάψιλα
evidence: Small sandy beach between Skala and Grikos with the warmest waters on Patmos; sources describe other Patmos beaches (Kampos, Petra) as organized but say nothing explicit about Sapsila facilities.

name: Παραλία Βάγια
evidence: Vagia Patmos: shade only from tamarisks; the cafe ('Vagia'/'Eftychia') is a few metres above the beach, not on it — no sunbeds/umbrellas mentioned anywhere.

name: Παραλία Λεύκες
evidence: Patmosweb on Lefkes: 'Λίγο πριν τον Κάμπο (Υπάρχει καντίνα)' — a canteen operates at the beach; no sunbeds/umbrellas mentioned.

name: Ψιλή άμμος
evidence: Psili Ammos Patmos 'does not have organized facilities, so you won't find umbrellas and loungers'; a small seasonal taverna operates on the sand (matches our 'ταβέρνα εποχικά').

name: Παραλία Αλυκή
evidence: No Rhodes-specific source found for an Alyki beach; all search results refer to Alyki/Alykes beaches on Paros, Thasos, Evia etc. (name collision).

name: Παραλία Ιξιάς
evidence: Ixia Rhodes 'είναι οργανωμένη στα περισσότερα τμήματά της, με beach bars, ομπρέλες και ξαπλώστρες' plus water-sports facilities.

name: Παραλία Κοπριά
evidence: Kopria (west Rhodes) 'does not have sun loungers, umbrellas or a canteen — you need to be self-organized'; only an aggregator site auto-claims facilities, which contradicts the guide sources.

name: Παραλία Φούρνοι
evidence: Fourni (Monolithos, Rhodes) is not organized overall but 'υπάρχει μια μικρή καντίνα' selling drinks/snacks, and one source also mentions umbrellas present.

name: Παραλία Γαλούνι
evidence: Only found that Galouni (south Rhodes) was among beaches auctioned by the municipality for water-sports concessions — no evidence of actual sunbeds/bar operating.

name: Σύμη Γυάλα
evidence: Gyala near Nimborio is listed among Symi beaches reachable by road, but no source explicitly states sunbeds/umbrellas or a bar at Gyala itself.

name: Χέλατρος
evidence: Chelatros Kasos 'has no organization — make sure to have the necessary equipment and supplies, as there is no shop within a radius of many kilometers'.

name: Παραλία Μαραθούντα
evidence: Marathounta on Pserimos: 'Η παραλία δεν είναι οργανωμένη' — sand/pebble beach by the gorge with a small jetty; access by boat, 4x4 or trail.

name: Μαράθι
evidence: Two seasonal tavernas operate on tiny Marathi by the beach (confirmed), and one blended result claims sunbeds are available, but no reliable source explicitly confirms sunbeds/umbrellas or a beach bar on the sand.

name: Πλαζ Πατρών
evidence: Plaz (EOT) Patras: all-day cafes/bars/restaurants offering sunbeds and umbrellas, lifeguard, disabled access — classified as an organized beach; also in the SEATRAC directory.

name: Mirtia Strand
evidence: No source found describing facilities at this coastal spot; searches for 'Μυρτιά Αιτωλοακαρνανία' return the inland Trichonida-lake village of Myrtia with lakeside tavernas, not a verifiable sea beach with sunbeds.

name: Μυρτιά
evidence: Same ambiguity as Mirtia Strand: results point to the Myrtia village on Lake Trichonida (waterside tavernas); no explicit evidence of sunbeds/umbrellas or a beach bar at this specific shore.

name: Παραθάλασσο
evidence: No source found referring to a beach named Parathalasso in Aetolia-Acarnania; nearby-area beach bars exist (e.g. Vathiavali) but nothing tied to this beach.
